climate.overview_html: IPCC-65 is now in its second day in Addis Ababa, with Chair Jim Skea confirming the session’s primary task is resolving the AR7 delivery-timeline deadlock for the sixth consecutive plenary. The 2026 Super El Niño continues to intensify: WMO projects Niño 3.4 averaging +3.7°C for October–December, far above the prior record of +2.6°C from November 2015. A University of Bristol & Lancet team published five priority actions for public-health emergency preparedness under the Super El Niño, citing infectious disease, malnutrition and heat-stress risks across Africa, Asia and South America through northern spring 2027. Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.) confirms Antarctic ice loss is “very likely” on all 2100 pathways; the UN Secretary-General insists “overshoot is not a reason to surrender” ahead of COP31 in Antalya, 9–20 November.

items.headline: WMO October 2026 El Niño Update: Niño 3.4 Observed +3.34°C (6 Oct), Projected +3.7°C Peak December — Would Be Strongest on Record; Central Pacific Exceeds 30°C for First Time; Near-100% Probability Through February 2027
items.summary: The WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update (October 7–8, 2026) reports the Niño 3.4 anomaly reached +3.34°C on October 6 and is projected to average approximately +3.7°C for October–December 2026, peaking around December — far above the prior record of +2.6°C from November 2015–January 2016. The central Pacific exceeded 30°C (86°F) for the first time in the continuous SST record. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo stated near-100% probability of persistence through February 2027. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole is expected to peak in October before declining. Compound drought–flood anomalies are forecast across Australasia, southern Africa, South America and South Asia through northern spring 2027.

items.headline: IPCC-65 Opens in Addis Ababa (12–16 Oct): Chair Skea Confirms AR7 Timeline Deadlock Persists; Sixth Consecutive Session Without Resolution; COP31 Virtual Consultation 14 October
items.summary: IPCC-65 opened on 12 October 2026 at the UN Economic Commission for Africa in Addis Ababa, running through 16 October. Chair Jim Skea confirmed the plenary will again attempt to resolve the AR7 delivery-timeline deadlock — unresolved across six consecutive sessions. Primary divide: one bloc (EU and small island states) presses for all three Working Group reports by mid-2028 to inform the 2028 Global Stocktake; a second bloc (including major emerging economies) seeks WG2 and WG3 deferred to 2029. The COP31 co-presidency (Turkey/Australia) scheduled a virtual consultation with IPCC delegates for 14 October. IPCC's trust fund is projected to be exhausted by end-2028 without new contributions.

items.headline: Bristol & Lancet: Five Priority Steps for Public-Health Emergency Preparedness Under 2026 Super El Niño; Infectious Disease, Malnutrition and Heat-Stress Risks Flagged Across Tropics and Subtropics
items.summary: A University of Bristol-led team published five priority preparedness steps in The Lancet for the 2026 Super El Niño's health impacts. The paper calls for (1) UN-coordinated public health emergency declaration, (2) national government health assessments and early-warning deployments, (3) scaled-up El Niño-focused climate-health attribution research, plus steps on malnutrition surveillance and heat-stress interventions. Health risks include accelerated spread of malaria, dengue, cholera and diarrhoeal diseases in flood-affected zones, malnutrition from drought-linked crop failure, and heat stress across tropical Africa, South Asia and South America. El Niño can be forecast months in advance — offering a preparation window the current record event should immediately trigger.

items.headline: COP31 Co-Presidency Circulates Draft Cover Decision Text; Türkiye and Australia Seek “Ambitious” Action Language; 1.5°C Framing, Fossil Fuel Phase-Out and Finance Pledges Remain Contested
items.summary: Turkey and Australia circulated draft COP31 cover decision text on October 8, building on the Fiji Pre-COP framework. Key fault lines: 1.5°C overshoot language; fossil fuel phase-out; and new finance pledges versus implementation of existing commitments. COP31 co-president Turkey's Murat Kurum called 1.5°C 'a matter of survival' for the Pacific. Turkey frames COP31 as an 'implementation COP' focused on delivering existing commitments rather than announcing new targets.

items.headline: EU Finalises COP31 Negotiating Position: Mitigation Work Programme to 2040; 2028 Global Stocktake Mechanism; “No Scope” for New Finance Pledges; Cites UNEP Finding 1.5°C To Be Exceeded
items.summary: The EU finalised its COP31 negotiating position on October 6, calling for extending the Mitigation Work Programme to at least 2040, establishing a 2028 Global Stocktake mechanism, and implementing existing commitments rather than making new finance pledges — the draft states there is 'no scope' for additional pledges at COP31. The position directly cites the UNEP Limiting Overshoot report, which concluded 1.5°C will likely be exceeded within a few years and that the most stringent Paris pathways 'are no longer feasible.'

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Highest-Ambition Paris Pathway Reduces Upper-End SLR ~50%; 95th-Percentile Very High Emissions: 25.4 cm by 2100
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study led by Rutgers climate scientist Robert Kopp finds Antarctic ice loss contributing to global sea-level rise by 2100 is 'very likely' under all studied emissions scenarios. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic SLR contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least 89% probability of producing less Antarctic ice loss by century's end.

items.headline: 2026 Arctic Sea Ice Minimum: 4.6 Million km² (12 Sep) — Tied 10th Lowest in 47 Years; All 20 Lowest Satellite-Era Summer Minima Occurred During 2007–2026
items.summary: NASA and NSIDC confirmed the 2026 Arctic sea ice minimum at approximately 4.6 million km² on September 12, tying 2008, 2010 and 2025 for the 10th lowest in 47 years — 1.21 million km² above the 2012 all-time record low. All 20 lowest Arctic summer minima in the satellite record have now occurred in the last 20 years (2007–2026), reflecting a roughly stable record-low regime established since the 2007 step-change.

major_events.name: Hurricane Simon (Eastern Pacific) — CATEGORY 2 (105 MPH / 170 KM/H); WEAKENED FROM CAT-4 PEAK; MOVING OFFSHORE BEFORE EXPECTED RETURN TO MEXICO’S PACIFIC COAST ~WEDNESDAY 14 OCTOBER; JALISCO–SINALOA CORRIDOR AT CONTINUED RISK; LIFE-THREATENING FLOODING ONGOING
major_events.status: ACTIVE, WEAKENING — Hurricane Simon has weakened to Category 2 with maximum sustained winds of approximately 105 mph (170 km/h), down from its Category 4 peak of 155 mph on Saturday; the storm has been tracking parallel to and slightly offshore Mexico’s Pacific coast rather than making a clean inland strike; NHC track projects Simon moving farther offshore Monday before turning back northeast toward Mexico’s coast around Wednesday 14 October, with Artemis noting Mexico’s cat bond parametric box has not yet been triggered; Jalisco–Sinaloa corridor faces a potential second heavy-rain event
major_events.impact: Life-threatening flooding and mudslides ongoing across Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán; 10–20 inches of rainfall broadly, isolated totals to 30 inches; class suspensions across 22 Jalisco coastal municipalities; evacuations ongoing in at-risk coastal communities; storm is expected to weaken further over cooler SSTs while offshore then potentially re-approach coast Wednesday–Thursday with diminished but still significant rainfall threat; final damage and casualty figures pending

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Haze — ONGOING; AERIAL FIREFIGHTING HAMPERED BY DENSE SMOG; SINGAPORE ANNOUNCES HAZE-ILLNESS MEDICAL SUBSIDIES; 60,000 FIREFIGHTERS DEPLOYED; SCHOOL CLOSURES ~2 MILLION STUDENTS
major_events.status: ONGOING — RESPONSE ENTERING NEW PHASE — Bloomberg (13 October) reports Indonesia’s aerial firefighting has been hampered for more than a week by the very haze it seeks to extinguish: dense smog has grounded water-bombing and cloud-seeding operations in Central Kalimantan, forcing reliance on 60,000 ground personnel; LiCAS.news (13 October) reports Singapore has announced government subsidies for medical treatment of haze-linked illnesses, and tens of thousands have fallen ill; conservationists have rescued dozens of orangutans trapped by smoke and flames; school closures affecting approximately 2 million students continue across Malaysia
major_events.impact: 60,000 Indonesian firefighters deployed across Sumatra and Kalimantan; aerial firefighting compromised by haze-related visibility; more than 200,000 hectares burned; more than 170,000 respiratory infection cases recorded in Indonesia; Singapore PSI at Very Unhealthy levels with government medical subsidies now in place; school closures affecting ~2 million students in Malaysia; bilateral Indonesia–Malaysia coordination elevated to PM/presidential level; ASEAN environment ministers' meeting still pending; El Niño-linked dry conditions in Borneo and South Sumatra are the primary driver of fire risk

major_events.name: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 27W) — COMPLETING EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION; WEAKENED TO ~75 KT (~140 KM/H); RECURVING NORTHEAST OVER OPEN NORTH PACIFIC; NO JAPAN MAINLAND THREAT
major_events.status: WEAKENING — EXTRATROPICAL TRANSITION IMMINENT — WeatherNews Japan places Koguma at approximately 140 km/h (~75 kt) as of 13 October, down from the 222 km/h (120 kt) JTWC confirmed on 10 October; latest track positions the system well east of Japan, recurving north-northeastward over cooler North Pacific SSTs; extratropical transition is projected to complete around 14 October; no typhoon watches or warnings are in effect for mainland Japan or the Marianas
major_events.impact: Elevated swell and storm-force seas east of Honsū and across the Ogasawara Islands; significant North Pacific swell propagating eastward once extratropical; shipping lane advisory in effect for east-coast Japan seas through mid-week; Koguma completes a historically notable October: three simultaneous Western Pacific tropical systems for the first time in five years, partly attributable to anomalously warm tropical Pacific SSTs from the 2026 Super El Niño

weather.overview_html: As of Tuesday 13 October, three simultaneous high-impact weather events remain active. Hurricane Simon has weakened to Category 2 (105 mph), down from its Category 4 peak, and is currently tracking offshore before an expected turn back toward Mexico’s coast around Wednesday 14 October — the Jalisco–Sinaloa corridor faces a potential second heavy-rain event. Bloomberg reports the Southeast Asian haze crisis has entered a new phase: dense smog is now actively preventing aerial firefighting and cloud-seeding in Central Kalimantan, and Singapore has announced medical treatment subsidies for haze-related illness. Typhoon Koguma has weakened to ~75 kt and is completing extratropical transition over the open North Pacific with no Japan mainland threat. Hurricane Isaias recovery in Florida has advanced to near-completion: FPL achieved its Monday restoration target with only rural Panhandle cooperative customers still affected.

items.headline: Hurricane Simon: Weakened to Category 2 (105 mph); Tracking Offshore Before Expected Return to Mexico’s Pacific Coast ~Wednesday 14 Oct; NHC Watching Jalisco–Sinaloa Corridor; Mexico Cat Bond Not Yet Triggered
items.summary: Hurricane Simon weakened from its Category 4 peak (155 mph, October 11) to Category 2 (approximately 105 mph / 170 km/h) by Monday October 12. The storm has been tracking parallel to and slightly offshore Mexico's Pacific coast rather than making a clean inland strike, reducing — but not eliminating — immediate landfall risk. The NHC track shows Simon moving farther offshore on Monday before turning back northeast toward the Mexican coast around Wednesday October 14; the Jalisco–Sinaloa corridor faces a potential second heavy-rain event. Artemis.bm analysis indicates Mexico's outstanding catastrophe bond parametric trigger box has not been formally activated, consistent with the storm's offshore trajectory. Life-threatening flooding and mudslides from the first passage continue across Jalisco, Colima, Nayarit and Michoacán — final rain totals and casualty figures remain pending.

items.headline: SE Asian Haze Day 14+: Dense Smog Prevents Aerial Firefighting and Cloud Seeding in Kalimantan; Singapore Announces Haze-Illness Medical Subsidies; Tens of Thousands Ill; Orangutan Rescues Ongoing
items.summary: Bloomberg reported on October 13, 2026 that Indonesia's aerial firefighting has been hampered for more than a week by the dense haze it seeks to extinguish — poor visibility has grounded water-bombing and cloud-seeding flights in Central Kalimantan on Borneo. Ground crews (60,000 personnel) remain the primary response. LiCAS.news (October 13) reports Singapore's government announced subsidies to offset medical costs for haze-related respiratory illness treatment. Tens of thousands have fallen ill across the region. Conservation organisations have rescued dozens of orangutans trapped by smoke and encroaching flames in Borneo. El Niño-linked dry conditions in Borneo and South Sumatra are identified as the primary meteorological driver.

items.headline: Typhoon Koguma (JTWC 27W): Weakened to ~75 kt (~140 km/h); Extratropical Transition Completing ~14 October; No Japan Mainland Threat; Significant North Pacific Swell Propagating East
items.summary: WeatherNews Japan and JTWC confirm Typhoon Koguma has weakened to approximately 75 knots (140 km/h) as of October 13, recurving north-northeastward over the open North Pacific, well east of Japan. Extratropical transition is projected to complete around October 14. No typhoon warnings or watches are in effect for mainland Japan, the Ryukyus or the Marianas. Significant swell is propagating eastward into the North Pacific basin. Koguma completes a historically notable October sequence: three simultaneous Western Pacific tropical systems for the first time in five years, a pattern partly attributable to anomalously warm equatorial Pacific SSTs from the 2026 Super El Niño.

items.headline: Hurricane Isaias Recovery: FPL Near-Full Restoration Achieved Monday 12 Oct; Rural Panhandle Cooperative Customers Targeted Tuesday; Death Toll 4 (FL/AL); 17,000 Workers from 29 States Completed Mission
items.summary: Florida Power & Light achieved near-full power restoration by end of day Monday October 12 as targeted, reducing outages from a post-landfall peak of approximately 700,000 customers to fewer than 100,000 — primarily electric cooperative customers in rural Florida Panhandle counties (CHELCO, which lost about 90% of its system, targeted Tuesday for full restoration). More than 17,000 utility workers from 29 states completed the FPL portion of the mission. The death toll remains at four: two in Florida, two in Alabama. FEMA disaster declarations remain active for Gulf Coast counties.

renewables.overview_html: India added 35.2 GW solar and 4.69 GW wind in the first nine months of 2026, pushing cumulative solar above 171 GW; Wood Mackenzie projects full-year solar above 50 GW. In Europe, Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs dissolved its key wind and solar industry-liaison division effective 2 October — a structural reversal of the team built during the Habeck era. Poland’s first offshore wind farm, Baltic Power (76 Vestas V236-15 MW turbines), completed all installations and is in final commissioning. Clearway broke ground on the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Missouri after closing $1.5 billion in financing; Grenergy closed US$460 million for 446 MW solar + 1.8 GWh storage in Chile; Power Grid Corporation of India completed the Lakadia II transmission SPV acquisition to support Gujarat’s 7,500 MW renewable zone.

items.headline: India Adds 35.2 GW Solar and 4.69 GW Wind in First Nine Months of 2026; Cumulative Solar Exceeds 171 GW; Wood Mackenzie Projects Full-Year Solar Above 50 GW; Record Annual Pace
items.summary: JMK Research and MNRE data published October 8, 2026 confirm India added 35.2 GW of solar and 4.69 GW of wind capacity in the first nine months of 2026, bringing cumulative installed solar capacity above 171 GW. Wood Mackenzie projects full-year solar installations will exceed 50 GW, surpassing the prior year's record of approximately 49 GW. India is on track to meet and potentially exceed its interim renewable energy targets ahead of 2030 goals.

items.headline: Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs Dissolves Key Wind and Solar Industry-Liaison Division Effective 2 October; Structural Reversal of Team Built During Habeck Era
items.summary: Germany's Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Energy dissolved its dedicated wind and solar industry-liaison division, effective October 2, 2026, Bloomberg reported on October 7. The division was established under former Economy Minister Robert Habeck to accelerate renewables permitting and coordinate between industry and government. The dissolution marks a structural reversal under the current government's ministry reorganisation. Wind and solar industry associations have expressed concern about reduced direct access to ministry decision-makers at a critical period for German renewables build-out.

items.headline: Baltic Power: Cadeler Completes All 76 Vestas V236-15 MW Turbine Installations at Poland’s First Offshore Wind Farm (1.1–1.2 GW); Final Commissioning Underway
items.summary: Cadeler announced October 7, 2026 the completion of all 76 turbine installations at Baltic Power — Poland's first offshore wind farm — using jack-up vessels Wind Osprey and Wind Mover. Turbines are 76 Vestas V236-15 MW units; capacity is reported as 1.1–1.2 GW. The farm is jointly owned by Northland Power and PKN Orlen under a 25-year contract-for-difference subsidy. Baltic Power delivered first power to Poland's grid in July 2026; the project is now in final commissioning.

items.headline: Norway Revises Utsira Nord Floating Wind Support Terms: Reduced Pre-FID Withdrawal Penalty, Earlier State Aid Payments; Total Cap Unchanged at NOK 35 Billion (~€3.3 Billion)
items.summary: Norway's government revised support terms for the Utsira Nord 500 MW floating wind project on October 9, 2026, via the 2027 state budget. The financial penalty for withdrawing before a final investment decision is reduced; part of state aid payments will be advanced earlier in the project lifecycle. The total support cap remains unchanged at NOK 35 billion (~€3.3 billion). Revisions are linked to increased uncertainty from the immature floating wind supply chain.

items.headline: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Financing for 446 MW Solar and 1.8 GWh Storage in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Consortium; Largest Grenergy Project Financing
items.summary: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on October 9, 2026 for the Algarrobal platform (242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh BESS) and the Palmas cluster (204 MW solar + 289 MWh BESS) in Chile. BNP Paribas coordinated; BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG, Santander and Bank of Nova Scotia participated. The deal is Grenergy's largest single project financing, bringing total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.headline: Clearway Energy Group Breaks Ground on 650 MW Swan Energy Center (Missouri) After Closing $1.5 Billion Financing; 20-Year Google PPA; CIBC/DNB/NAB Consortium; Target COD 2028
items.summary: Clearway Energy Group closed $1.5 billion in project financing and commenced construction on the 650 MW Swan Energy Center in Bates County, Missouri on October 7, 2026. Banking consortium: CIBC, DNB Bank and National Australia Bank. The project carries a 20-year PPA with Google, with Blattner Energy as construction partner. Target commercial operations 2028; project generates more than $80 million for local schools via PILOT agreement.

items.headline: RWE Completes Sale of 33.33% Stake in Five Estuaries Offshore Wind (1.1 GW Consented, UK) to EDF; EDF Assumes Lead Developer Role; No Financial Terms Disclosed
items.summary: RWE completed the transfer of its 33.33% ownership stake in the Five Estuaries UK offshore wind project to EDF Power Solutions UK and Ireland on October 8, 2026. EDF will now lead the joint venture. Five Estuaries received development consent in December 2025; the project is consented at up to 79 turbines, ~1.1 GW, in the southern North Sea. RWE will reinvest proceeds into its existing consented offshore wind portfolio.

items.source: SolarQuarter / Power Grid Corporation of India
items.headline: Power Grid Corporation of India Acquires Lakadia II Transmission Project SPV from REC Power Development; Supports Gujarat’s 7,500 MW Renewable Energy Zone
items.summary: Power Grid Corporation of India completed the acquisition of the Lakadia II transmission project special purpose vehicle from REC Power Development and Consultancy on October 12, 2026. The project forms part of the green energy corridor supporting Gujarat's planned 7,500 MW renewable energy zone. Power Grid will own and operate the transmission assets interconnecting large-scale solar and wind generation in Gujarat to the national grid.

science.overview_html: Beucler et al.’s 13-author review (arXiv:2610.09770, submitted to Science Advances) identifies explicit external-forcing representation as the critical gap between AI weather and climate timescales, and notes AI weather models risk underperforming on unprecedented extremes outside their training distribution. FastNet v1.0 (Met Office / Alan Turing Institute) addresses the endemic front-blurring problem in data-driven models by embedding physical consistency constraints during training. A University of Bristol team published five El Niño health-preparedness steps in The Lancet. Kopp et al. in Nature Geoscience confirm Antarctic SLR is “very likely” on all 2100 pathways; a PNAS meta-analysis of 20,736 tipping-point papers finds permafrost abrupt thaw covered in only 0.7% of the literature vs. 20% for Greenland.

items.headline: Artificial Intelligence Pathways from Weather to Climate (arXiv:2610.09770, Beucler et al.): Explicit External Forcing Required to Bridge Forecast and Climate Timescales; AI Models Risk Underperforming on Unprecedented Extremes; 13-Author Review Submitted to Science Advances
items.meta: Tom Beucler, David Neelin, Hui Su, Ignacio Lopez-Gomez, Chris Bretherton, Oliver Watt-Meyer, Tapio Schneider, Costa Christopoulos, Will Chapman, Laure Zanna, Aditya Grover, Adam Subel et al. (UNIL/UCLA/Google Research/Caltech/NYU/AI2/UC Boulder) · arXiv:2610.09770 (physics.ao-ph, cs.AI, cs.LG) · Submitted to Science Advances 7 October 2026
items.summary: Beucler et al. identify the critical gap between weather and climate AI: models must represent external forcings (greenhouse gases, aerosols, land-use change) explicitly before medium-range forecast gains can extend to climate projection skill. Key findings: AI models are not intrinsically more efficient than GPU-ported dynamical models once architectural complexity is accounted for; data-driven models have recently approached dynamical models on subseasonal timescales (~1 month) in probabilistic benchmarks; but AI weather models risk underperforming dynamical models on unprecedented, record-breaking extremes not seen during training — a critical vulnerability for Super El Niño forecasting applications.

items.headline: FastNet v1.0: Met Office–Turing GNN Embeds Physical Consistency Constraints During Training; Matches or Exceeds Met Office Global Model; Addresses Front-Blurring Endemic to Data-Driven Models; Validated Against Hurricane Ian and Storm Ciarán
items.meta: Met Office / Alan Turing Institute · arXiv:2509.17658 (physics.ao-ph) · Published October 2026
items.summary: FastNet v1.0 is a graph neural network that embeds physical consistency constraints during training rather than as post-hoc corrections, directly addressing the sharp-fronts blurring endemic to pure data-driven AI weather models. It matches the Met Office Global Model on most metrics at tens of thousands of times the inference speed. Validation against Hurricane Ian (2022) and Storm Ciarán (2023) shows more realistic storm core structures and improved pressure–wind relationships.

items.headline: Bristol & Lancet: Five Priority Steps for Public-Health Emergency Preparedness Under the 2026 Super El Niño; Malaria, Dengue, Cholera, Malnutrition and Heat-Stress Risks Flagged Across Tropics and Subtropics
items.summary: A University of Bristol-led team published five priority health preparedness steps in The Lancet for the 2026 Super El Niño. The paper calls for: (1) UN-coordinated public health emergency declaration; (2) national government health assessments and early-warning system deployments; (3) scaled-up El Niño-focused climate-health attribution research; plus steps on malnutrition surveillance and heat-stress interventions. Identified risks include accelerated transmission of malaria, dengue, cholera and diarrhoeal diseases in flood-affected zones; malnutrition from drought-linked crop failure across sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia; and heat stress across tropical regions through northern spring 2027. The authors note El Niño forecasts months in advance provide a preparation window the current record event should immediately trigger.

items.headline: Nature Feature: “Are We Really Headed for a ‘Super’ El Niño? What the Science Says” — Reviews Model Agreement, Uncertainty Bounds and Expected Teleconnections for 2026–27
items.summary: A Nature feature reviews the scientific basis for the 2026 Super El Niño designation: model agreement underpinning the WMO's +3.7°C Niño 3.4 projection, where residual uncertainty lies, and how expected teleconnections (drought in Australasia and southern Africa; flooding in South America and the Horn of Africa; warmer European winters) are likely to play out through northern spring 2027. The article addresses the superposition of El Niño forcing with the long-term greenhouse warming trend, and what that means for expected 2026–27 global temperature records.

items.headline: Nature Geoscience (Kopp et al.): Antarctic Ice Loss “Very Likely” on All 2100 Emissions Pathways; Highest-Ambition Paris Pathway Halves Upper-End SLR vs. Very High Emissions; 95th Percentile Very High: 25.4 cm by 2100
items.meta: Robert Kopp et al. (Rutgers University RCEI) · Nature Geoscience · Published October 2026
items.summary: A Nature Geoscience study (Kopp et al., Rutgers) finds Antarctic ice loss contributing to global sea-level rise by 2100 is 'very likely' under all studied emissions scenarios. Under very high emissions, the 95th-percentile Antarctic SLR contribution reaches 25.4 cm by 2100 (median 15.7 cm). The highest-ambition Paris-consistent pathway carries at least 89% probability of producing less Antarctic ice loss by century's end, reducing the upper-end contribution by roughly half. Near-term emissions choices still meaningfully bound long-term Antarctic SLR risk despite committed ice loss being unavoidable.

items.headline: PNAS Meta-Analysis (20,736 Papers): Greenland Dominates Tipping Research (20%); Permafrost Abrupt Thaw Covered in Only 0.7%; Structural Scientific Attention Disparity May Skew Policy Prioritisation
items.summary: A PNAS meta-analysis of 20,736 publications on 14 climate tipping elements found the Greenland ice sheet appearing in 4,141 papers (20%). By contrast, abrupt thaw of permafrost in boreal forests appeared in only 139 papers (0.7%). High-risk tipping elements including permafrost carbon feedback and West African monsoon shifts are substantially understudied relative to their potential climate impact, creating a potential structural bias in the evidence base informing climate policy.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: Temperate Local Extinctions from Climate Change Now Outpacing Tropical Extinctions; Greater Climate Velocity at Mid-Latitudes Drives Faster Species Loss; Challenges Dominant Biodiversity-Risk Framing
items.summary: A Nature Climate Change study published October 6, 2026 reports that climate-driven local species extinctions are now occurring at a faster rate in temperate regions than in the tropics — an empirical reversal of the dominant paradigm. The authors attribute this to greater climate velocity in temperate zones under current warming, which species with limited dispersal ability cannot track. The finding has direct implications for conservation policy in Europe, North America and East Asia, which have focused biodiversity protection resources disproportionately on tropical ecosystems.

items.source: VU Amsterdam / TU Delft / University of Amsterdam / EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.headline: Xaurora: Probabilistic Generative Ensemble Forecasting via Stochastic Interpolants on Microsoft Aurora Foundation Model; Competitive with DLWP Ensembles at Fraction of Training Cost via LoRA Fine-Tuning
items.meta: VU Amsterdam, TU Delft, University of Amsterdam · EMS Annual Meeting 2026
items.summary: Xaurora converts Microsoft's deterministic Aurora foundation model into a fully generative stochastic ensemble system using the stochastic interpolant framework and LoRA fine-tuning. Results are competitive with state-of-the-art NWP ensembles and other data-driven approaches at a fraction of training cost, providing a practical pathway for converting any pre-trained deterministic weather foundation model into a probabilistic ensemble system without full retraining.

items.title: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners Acquires 25% Stake in Five Estuaries Offshore Wind (1.1 GW Consented, UK) from Macquarie-Led Consortium; Second Major Ownership Change at Same Project in Five Days
items.body_html: Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners (CIP) announced on 13 October 2026 that it has acquired the 25% stake in the Five Estuaries offshore wind project held by the Macquarie-led consortium. The acquisition follows RWE’s sale of its 33.33% developer stake to EDF on 8 October, marking the second significant ownership change at the consented 1.1 GW southern North Sea project within five days. The remaining partners are EDF Power Solutions (33.33%, now lead developer), ESB (20.83%) and Sumitomo Corporation (20.83%). Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.title: WindBorne Systems Wins Hefty US Air Force Contract for Balloon Weather Data; Total Government Value Could Reach ~$50 Million; Builds on $37 Million Series B (Aug 2026)
items.body_html: TechCrunch reports (12 October 2026) that WindBorne Systems won a US Air Force contract for its long-duration balloon atmospheric data, with the total government contract value potentially reaching approximately $50 million. WindBorne operates a constellation of roughly 600 long-duration weather balloons from 20 global launch sites; its AI-driven forecast models ingest the data for numerical weather prediction. The company raised a $37 million Series B in August 2026 led by Khosla Ventures and Galvanize at a $250 million valuation; the Air Force contract adds significant non-dilutive government revenue to its commercial data-as-a-service business.

items.title: Grenergy Closes ~US$460 Million Non-Recourse Senior Financing for 446 MW Solar + 1.8 GWh Storage Portfolio in Chile; BNP Paribas-Led Six-Bank Consortium; Total Chilean Non-Recourse Debt Exceeds US$2.4 Billion
items.body_html: Grenergy closed approximately US$460 million in non-recourse senior financing on 9 October 2026 for the Algarrobal platform (fifth phase of Oasis de Atacama: 242 MW solar + 1.5 GWh BESS) and the Palmas cluster (21 DG projects: 204 MW solar + 289 MWh BESS) in Chile. BNP Paribas coordinated and underwrote; BBVA, J.P. Morgan Chase, MUFG Bank, Santander and Bank of Nova Scotia co-participated. The deal is Grenergy’s largest single project financing, bringing its total Chilean non-recourse debt beyond US$2.4 billion.

items.title: RWE Completes Sale of 33.33% Stake in Five Estuaries UK Offshore Wind (1.1 GW Consented) to EDF; EDF Assumes Lead Developer Role; No Terms Disclosed
items.body_html: RWE Offshore Wind GmbH completed the transfer of its 33.33% stake in the Five Estuaries offshore wind project to EDF Power Solutions UK and Ireland on 8 October 2026. EDF will now lead the joint venture for the project (development consent December 2025; up to 79 turbines at ~1.1 GW, southern North Sea, extension of the Galloper wind farm off Suffolk). RWE stated proceeds will be reinvested in other consented offshore wind projects. Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.title: Sonnedix Acquires 54 MW Italy Solar Portfolio from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II (Macchiareddu, Sardinia + Aprilia, Lazio); Italian Operating Capacity Exceeds 1.3 GW
items.body_html: Sonnedix acquired two solar PV assets totalling 54 MW from EOS ReNewable Infrastructure Fund II on 7 October 2026: Macchiareddu (46.5 MW, Sardinia) and Aprilia (7.5 MW, Lazio), financed by a European bank consortium. The transaction lifts Sonnedix’s Italian operational portfolio above 1.3 GW — its third Italian acquisition in 2026 following a 194 MW portfolio in March and a 260 MW Tuscania battery storage portfolio in July.
